transcript.text: Hello, I'm here to help you get ready for your appointment. Could you tell me what has been bothering you?
Well, I keep getting this funny dizzy feeling when I stand up — it comes over me and I feel light-headed, like I might faint. It's been going on for a little while now.
When did you first notice it?
Oh, I'm not sure exactly — a while back now. It sort of crept up on me.
Is there anything that makes it better or worse?
It's worse first thing in the morning, when I get out of bed, or if I stand up quickly. If I sit back down for a minute it settles again.
How would you describe the feeling in your own words?
It's more of a swimmy, woozy feeling — like I'm about to faint — not the room spinning round, if that makes sense.
Where exactly do you feel it, and does it spread anywhere?
It's just a general feeling in my head really — I haven't noticed it spreading anywhere.
On a scale from 0 to 10, where 10 is the worst, how bad is it?
Oh, I wouldn't put a number on it really — it's not too bad, but it's enough to make me grab hold of something.
Is it there all the time, or does it come and go?
It comes and goes — I'm not dizzy all the time, it just catches me now and then.
Has anything else been bothering you along with this?
No, nothing else — no chest pain or anything like that. Just the dizzy turns.
Do you see a doctor regularly for any health condition?
Yes, I've had high blood pressure for years — about 15 years now. And I've got arthritis in both my hips, which is why I take the painkillers.
Which medicines do you take regularly, including any new ones?

Well, I take a water tablet every morning — have done for years — and some painkillers for my hips. There's a small tablet I take for my stomach too, and I've just started a new one for my blood pressure.
Are you allergic to any medicines?
No, not that I know of — I've never had a reaction to anything.
Has this changed what you can do around the house or outside?
I've stopped going to my Tuesday lunch club, actually — I'm worried about feeling faint on the bus. That's a shame, I did enjoy it.
Is there anything about this that worries you?
I do wonder if it's that new blood pressure tablet causing it. I'd like to know whether I should stop taking it.
Thank you, that is very helpful. I have put together a short summary of what you told me. Please read it and tell me if anything should be corrected before it goes to your doctor.
